newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Russian Far East mining said plagued by problems.
newsitem.headline: Russian Far East mining said plagued by problems.

text.p: The Russian Far East holds an overwhelming amount of minerals, but problems plague the development of the industry, a Russian economist said on Wednesday.
Pavel Minakir, director of the Economic Research Institute of the Academy of Sciences in the Russian Far East, told a mining conference the region contained more than 70 types of mineral resources.
"It has more than 80 percent of the Russian reserves of diamonds, 95 percent of tin, 90 percent of boron, 88 percent of antimony...and significant reserves of gold and silver," Minakir said.
There are also substantial reserves of aluminiu, titanium, mercury, fluorspar, tungsten, oil and natural gas.

But investment was needed badly to develop these resources because of deficient laws, inadequate infrastructure and crafting of incentives as attractive as those that exist in the booming countries along the Asia-Pacific rim, Minakir said.

"The only real way of improving the investment climate in the Far East is to grant greater self-sufficiency and certain preferences to the region in the sphere of external economic relations, including the question of attracting foreign capital," Minakir said.
The economist urged the federal government in Moscow to take steps to help regional governments in luring investments to the mining industry.
